title: Overtaking: who keeps clear? COLREG Rule 13 explained

scenes.label: WHO GIVES WAY?
scenes.heading: Overtaking? You keep clear.
scenes.narration: You are faster, and coming up astern of another ship. Who keeps out of the way?

scenes.label: RULE 13
scenes.heading: The overtaking vessel keeps out of the way
scenes.narration: A vessel is overtaking when she comes up from more than 22.5 degrees abaft the other vessel's beam. By night, she would see only the sternlight. Rule 13 says any vessel overtaking must keep out of the way of the vessel being overtaken.

scenes.label: WHAT THE RULES REQUIRE
scenes.heading: Three points officers forget

items.title: It applies to every vessel
items.text: Even a sailing vessel overtaking a power-driven ship

items.title: In doubt? You are overtaking
items.text: Rule 13(c): assume it and act accordingly

items.title: Once overtaking, always overtaking
items.text: Until you are finally past and clear

scenes.narration: Three points. This rule applies to every vessel, even a sailing vessel overtaking a power-driven ship. If you are in doubt, assume you are overtaking. And a later change of bearing does not make you a crossing vessel: you keep clear until you are finally past and clear.

scenes.label: KEY TAKEAWAY
scenes.heading: Overtaking? Keep clear until past and clear.
scenes.narration: Coming up from astern? Keep clear, until you are past and clear.
